_comment: Run from packages/gateway (pnpm --filter @theokit/gateway run test:mutation); deliberately NOT wired into `test`, so `pnpm -r run test` in CI never pays for it. configFile points at vitest.mutation.config.ts, which drops tests/lint/** — those suites walk the monorepo tree from the repo root (__dirname/../../../..) and break inside Stryker's sandbox, and they READ source text rather than executing it, so they could never kill a mutant of these two files anyway. related:false because tests live in a mirror tree (tests/**) and vitest --related cannot map a source file back to them. inPlace is deliberately unset: the sandbox works once the lint suites are excluded, and the working tree is never mutated in place. mutate is scoped to the two files with real branching logic that only unit tests cover — both chunkers and the hook chain; src/hooks/types.ts is types-only and has nothing to mutate. thresholds.break=93 is the MEASURED baseline with headroom for one mutant (93.35% on 2026-08-29; one mutant is 0.25% of 406). READ THIS BEFORE COMPARING IT TO AN OLDER NUMBER: it is not a drop from the 94.35% recorded earlier the same day. That figure was over TWO files; this one is over four, and the two added arrived with 65 survivors between them. Scoring less of the code higher is not a better suite, so the scope moved and the floor moved with it -- which is the one case where lowering break is honest, and it is honest only because the change is stated here. It makes the score a ratchet: a real regression fails the run, with roughly one mutant of headroom. Only the killed/timeout split moved between runs, and a timeout scores as killed. Raise break when the score rises; never lower it to make a red run green.\n\nThe remaining 10 survivors are EQUIVALENT MUTANTS -- no test can kill them because none of them changes behaviour, and writing a test that appears to would be writing for the scoreboard. They are listed so the next reader does not re-derive it: chunk.ts L85 (`cut >= text.length`, both forms) -- past the end `charCodeAt` yields NaN and every comparison against it is false, so the early return and the fall-through agree; L99 (`cut > 0` -> `>= 0`) -- at cut===0 the mutant keeps 0 and L102 then returns `window`, which is what the original returns directly; L102 (`cut <= 0`, both forms) -- cut is `window` or a positive boundary by then, so 0 is unreachable and the check is defensive; L114 (`\"window\"` -> `\"\"`) -- the value is only ever compared against `\"last-boundary\"` and both fail it; L171 (`text.length === 0` -> false) -- an empty string falls to `text.length <= limit` and returns `[\"\"]` by the other path; L174 (`{granularity:\"grapheme\"}` -> `{}`) -- grapheme IS Intl.Segmenter's default granularity; L184 (`buf.length > 0`, both forms) -- the loop always appends a segment before reaching it, so buf is never empty there. For chunk.ts that puts the ceiling at 92.6%. credential-patterns.ts is at its own ceiling of 98.0%: its two survivors are the `typeof value === \"string\" ? value : String(value)` ternary, where `String(s)` IS `s` for a string, so neither branch selection can change the result. gateway-runner.ts still has 15 survivors that have NOT been shown to be equivalent -- outstanding work, not a ceiling.
